senses.gloss: The general direction in which opinion or events are moving.
examples: The *tide* of public opinion turned against the war.
Two early wins turned the *tide* for the team.
He was swimming against the *tide* of company policy.

senses.gloss: A result in which two players or teams finish with the same score.
examples: The game ended in a 2-2 *tie*.
A *tie* in the first round means they play again on Friday.
Both runners crossed the line together, so the judges called it a *tie*.

senses.gloss: A close connection or relationship between people, groups, or countries.
examples: She still has strong family *ties* in Ohio.
The two countries have close economic *ties*.
He cut every *tie* with his old firm.

senses.gloss: One of the heavy wooden beams that a railroad track is laid across.
examples: The crew replaced a hundred rotten *ties* last summer.
We edged the flower bed with old railroad *ties*.
He counted the *ties* as he walked along the track.

senses.gloss: One of several levels in a system, each ranked above or below the others.
examples: The basic plan is the cheapest *tier* of service.
She moved up to the top *tier* of management.
The league has three *tiers*, and the bottom teams drop down.

senses.gloss: A small flat piece used as a playing piece in certain games.
examples: He drew seven *tiles* from the Scrabble bag.
One *tile* was missing from the game box.
She turned her *tiles* face down at the end of the round.

senses.gloss: The bar attached to a boat's rudder that you push to steer.
examples: He kept one hand on the *tiller* and one on the sail.
Push the *tiller* left and the bow swings right.
The old wooden *tiller* was worn smooth.

senses.gloss: A short period in which a child has to sit quietly alone as a punishment.
examples: Her son got a five-minute *timeout* for hitting his sister.
He spent the whole *timeout* on the bottom stair.
*Timeouts* work better than yelling, the book says.

senses.gloss: The point at which a computer or phone stops waiting for a response and gives up.
examples: The upload failed with a *timeout*.
Set the *timeout* to thirty seconds.
Slow servers cause a lot of *timeouts*.

senses.gloss: The particular moment at which something happens or is done.
examples: The *timing* of the announcement surprised everyone.
The *timing* of the layoffs, right before the holidays, made people angry.
The *timing* of the two storms was pure coincidence.

senses.gloss: A metal container with a lid, used for food such as cookies or candy.
examples: She keeps her cookies in a big red *tin*.
There's a *tin* of shortbread on the counter.
He used an old candy *tin* to hold his buttons.

senses.gloss: A shallow metal pan used for baking.
examples: Grease the muffin *tin* before you pour in the batter.
The pie cooled in its *tin* on the windowsill.
She stacked the baking *tins* under the counter.

senses.gloss: The pointed or narrow end of something.
examples: The *tip* of my nose was red from the cold.
He broke the *tip* off the pencil.
Only the *tip* of the iceberg shows above the water.

senses.gloss: A small piece of practical advice.
examples: She gave me a few *tips* on interviewing.
Here's a *tip*: soak the pan overnight.
The website is full of gardening *tips*.

senses.gloss: A piece of secret information given to the police or the press.
examples: An anonymous *tip* led police to the warehouse.
The reporter got a *tip* about the mayor's meeting.
Detectives followed up on dozens of *tips*.

senses.gloss: A word used before someone's name or for a position, showing rank or job.
examples: Her official *title* is director of research.
He was given the *title* of duke.
People with fancy *titles* don't always do much work.

senses.gloss: The legal right to own something, or the document that proves it.
examples: You can't sell the car without the *title*.
The bank holds the *title* until the loan is paid off.
They found a problem with the *title* to the land.

senses.gloss: The position of champion in a sport.
examples: She won her third *title* in a row.
The team hasn't taken the *title* since 1994.
He defends his *title* in Las Vegas next month.

senses.gloss: The part of a shoe or sock that covers the toes.
examples: There's a hole in the *toe* of my sock.
These work boots have a steel *toe*.
The *toe* of his sneaker was scuffed.

senses.gloss: The total damage or number of deaths caused by something bad.
examples: The death *toll* from the earthquake rose to 300.
Years of night shifts took a *toll* on his health.
The storm's *toll* on local farms was enormous.

senses.gloss: A very large amount or number.
examples: I have a *ton* of homework tonight.
They spent *tons* of money on the wedding.
There were *tons* of people at the fair.

senses.gloss: The quality of a voice or piece of writing that shows the speaker's feeling or attitude.
examples: Don't take that *tone* with me.
Her email had a friendly *tone*.
He apologized in a serious *tone*.

senses.gloss: A single electronic sound, such as the beep before you leave a message.
examples: Please leave your message after the *tone*.
There was no dial *tone* when I picked up the phone.
The elevator gives a soft *tone* at each floor.

senses.gloss: A language, especially the one a person grew up speaking.
examples: Spanish is her native *tongue*.
He can argue in three *tongues*.
The old prayers are still said in the mother *tongue*.

senses.gloss: The flap of leather or cloth under the laces of a shoe.
examples: Pull the *tongue* straight before you tie the laces.
The *tongue* of the boot was padded.
His sneakers have the brand name on the *tongue*.

senses.gloss: Something that makes you feel stronger, healthier, or more cheerful.
examples: A week at the lake was a real *tonic*.
Her visit was a *tonic* for the whole family.
The doctor prescribed a *tonic* to build up his strength.

senses.gloss: Anything used as a means of doing a job or getting a result.
examples: Language is a writer's most important *tool*.
The app is a useful *tool* for tracking spending.
Taxes are a blunt *tool* for fixing the housing market.

senses.gloss: A piece of clothing worn on the upper half of the body.
examples: She wore a black *top* with jeans.
I need a *top* that goes with this skirt.
All the summer *tops* were on sale.

senses.gloss: The lid or cap that closes a container.
examples: I can't get the *top* off this jar.
Put the *top* back on the marker so it doesn't dry out.
The bottle *top* rolled under the table.

senses.gloss: A toy that spins on a point when you twist or pull it.
examples: The little wooden *top* spun for almost a minute.
He wound the string around the *top* and let it go.
She got a set of painted *tops* for her birthday.

senses.gloss: A stick with a flame burning at one end, carried for light or ceremony.
examples: Runners carried the Olympic *torch* through town.
*Torches* lit the path down to the barn.
The guide held a *torch* above his head in the cave.

senses.gloss: A very small amount of something added.
examples: The soup needs a *touch* of salt.
There's a *touch* of gray at his temples.
Add a *touch* of lemon to the sauce.

senses.gloss: A person's own special skill or way of doing something.
examples: She has a wonderful *touch* with nervous horses.
After twenty years the pitcher has lost his *touch*.
A few flowers gave the room a personal *touch*.

senses.gloss: Contact or communication with someone.
examples: Let's keep in *touch* after graduation.
I lost *touch* with most of my classmates.
Get in *touch* with me when you land.

senses.gloss: A series of performances or games given in different places.
examples: The band is on *tour* in Europe this fall.
She played forty cities on her last *tour*.
The *tour* ends with two nights in Chicago.

senses.gloss: A fixed period of duty served in one place, especially by a soldier.
examples: He served two *tours* in Afghanistan.
Her *tour* lasted thirteen months.
He came home between *tours*.

senses.gloss: A single song or piece of music on an album.
examples: The third *track* is my favorite.
The album has twelve *tracks*.
They released one *track* early as a single.

senses.gloss: A course, usually oval, for running or racing.
examples: She runs four miles on the *track* every morning.
The horses came around the far turn of the *track*.
Our school just resurfaced the *track*.

senses.gloss: A line of marks left on the ground by an animal, person, or vehicle.
examples: There were deer *tracks* in the snow.
Muddy *tracks* led from the door to the garage.
The hunter followed the bear's *tracks* for a mile.

senses.gloss: A system of connected organs that something passes through in the body.
examples: Fiber keeps the digestive *tract* healthy.
The infection spread to her upper respiratory *tract*.
The drug is absorbed in the intestinal *tract*.

senses.gloss: A short printed pamphlet arguing a religious or political point.
examples: A man on the corner handed out religious *tracts*.
The *tract* ran to only eight pages.
He published a *tract* against the new tax.

senses.gloss: An exchange in which each side gives something and gets something back.
examples: The Yankees got two pitchers in the *trade*.
I gave him my sandwich for his chips, an even *trade*.
It was a fair *trade*: he fixed my car and I painted his fence.

senses.gloss: A very sad event, especially one in which people die.
examples: The fire was a *tragedy* for the whole town.
It would be a *tragedy* to lose the old theater.
The family has suffered two *tragedies* in one year.

senses.gloss: A line of marks, smells, or objects left behind that can be followed.
examples: The dog picked up the *trail* near the creek.
He left a *trail* of muddy footprints down the hall.
Investigators followed a paper *trail* to the account.

senses.gloss: A short set of clips advertising a movie or show before it comes out.
examples: The *trailer* looked better than the movie.
They showed four *trailers* before the film started.
The studio put the first *trailer* online yesterday.

senses.gloss: A long low home built to be hauled to a lot and lived in.
examples: They live in a *trailer* just outside of town.
The storm flattened half the *trailers* in the park.
She grew up in a two-bedroom *trailer*.

senses.gloss: The long part of a gown that trails on the ground behind the wearer.
examples: Two girls carried the bride's *train*.
Her gown had a six-foot *train*.
He stepped on the *train* of her dress.

senses.gloss: A series of connected thoughts or events.
examples: The phone rang and I lost my *train* of thought.
The letter set off a *train* of events no one expected.
A long *train* of small mistakes led to the crash.

senses.gloss: A small open vehicle that carries people short distances at an airport, park, or resort.
examples: Take the *tram* from the parking lot to the terminal.
We rode the *tram* around the zoo.
The *tram* stops at every hotel on the strip.

senses.gloss: Something of very poor quality.
examples: That movie was total *trash*.
He says most of the songs on the radio are *trash*.
The book got great reviews, but I thought it was *trash*.

senses.gloss: A serious physical injury to the body.
examples: He died of blunt force *trauma* to the head.
The hospital has a level-one *trauma* center.
She suffered severe *trauma* to her left leg in the crash.

senses.gloss: Something enjoyable that is out of the ordinary, often paid for by someone else.
examples: Lunch is my *treat* today.
Going to the movies was a rare *treat* for us.
As a *treat*, he took the kids to the ballpark.

senses.gloss: A small sweet food, especially one given to children.
examples: The kids came home with a bag of Halloween *treats*.
She baked *treats* for the whole class.
One *treat* after dinner, that's the rule.

senses.gloss: A diagram that branches out to show how things are connected.
examples: She traced the family *tree* back to 1820.
The lawyer drew a *tree* showing who inherits what.
Each choice adds another branch to the decision *tree*.

senses.gloss: A slight uncontrollable shaking of the body or voice.
examples: There was a *tremor* in her voice as she read the letter.
The medication reduced the *tremor* in his hands.
A *tremor* ran through him when he heard the news.

senses.gloss: A long narrow hole dug in the ground for pipes, cables, or drainage.
examples: The crew dug a *trench* for the water line.
Don't fall in the *trench* they cut across the driveway.
Gravel goes in the bottom of the *trench*.

senses.gloss: A very deep narrow valley in the ocean floor.
examples: The Pacific has the deepest *trenches* on earth.
Strange creatures live at the bottom of the *trench*.
The submarine descended slowly into the *trench*.

senses.gloss: A general change or direction of development over a period of time.
examples: There's an upward *trend* in gas prices.
The *trend* toward working from home has continued.
Test scores show a worrying *trend*.

senses.gloss: A payment made by one ruler or country to a stronger one.
examples: The conquered towns paid *tribute* to Rome every year.
The king demanded *tribute* in gold and grain.
Refusing to send *tribute* meant war.

senses.gloss: A clever method that makes something easier to do.
examples: The *trick* is to add the eggs slowly.
There's a *trick* to opening that window.
She showed me a few *tricks* for saving battery.

senses.gloss: Something that causes another thing to start or happen.
examples: Stress is a common *trigger* for migraines.
The arrest was the *trigger* for weeks of protests.
Certain foods are *triggers* for her allergy.

senses.gloss: A light cutting that makes hair or a hedge neat without changing it much.
examples: I just want a *trim*, not a new style.
The hedge needs a *trim* before the party.
A quick *trim* costs twenty dollars here.

senses.gloss: The narrow strips of wood around the doors, windows, and floor of a room.
examples: We painted the walls gray and the *trim* white.
The *trim* around the window is rotting.
New *trim* would make the room look finished.

senses.gloss: A powered garden tool for cutting hedges or the edges of a lawn.
examples: He edged the sidewalk with a string *trimmer*.
The hedge *trimmer* needs a new blade.
She ran the *trimmer* along the fence line.

senses.gloss: An ugly creature in old northern European stories, said to live in caves or under bridges.
examples: In the story, a *troll* guards the bridge.
The kids drew *trolls* with huge noses.
He read them a tale about a *troll* who turned to stone in the sun.

senses.gloss: The low point in a cycle, between two high points.
examples: The economy hit a *trough* in early spring.
Sales rise in December and fall to a *trough* in July.
The boat rose on the crest and dropped into the *trough*.

senses.gloss: A flat-bladed hand tool used to spread mortar, cement, or plaster.
examples: The bricklayer scooped mortar with his *trowel*.
Smooth the patch with a wide *trowel*.
He cleaned the *trowel* before the cement dried.

senses.gloss: A small powerful boat that pushes and pulls larger ships.
examples: Two *tugs* guided the tanker into the harbor.
The *tug* blew its horn twice.
A *tug* pushed the loaded barge upriver.

senses.gloss: An acrobat who does rolls, flips, and handsprings.
examples: A line of *tumblers* came out before the clowns.
She was the best *tumbler* on the gymnastics team.
The *tumblers* finished with a triple flip.

senses.gloss: One of the small parts inside a lock that the key has to move before it opens.
examples: He listened for the *tumblers* to click.
A worn key won't lift all the *tumblers*.
The locksmith explained how the *tumblers* line up.

senses.gloss: The rotating structure on a tank, ship, or aircraft that holds a gun.
examples: The tank's *turret* swung slowly to the right.
A shell struck the forward *turret*.
The gunner sat in a glass *turret* under the plane.
